title: Field install coda — weekly notes & escalations (Nov 8–10, 2026)
content:
Summary:
This note captures the install cadence, recent customer-facing regressions, and immediate mitigations for the Nov 8–10 field installs. Focused on two active engagements (Acadia Health and QubitRetail) where we saw flaky post-install smoke tests, intermittent KV-cache warm failures, and one kernel/driver mismatch that forced a rollback on a 3090 node pool.

Purpose / audience:
- Working notes for eng-private-deployments leads, SRE on-call, solutions-eng (customer handoff) and install field engineers.
- Triage history + short-term action items to hand to the weekday shift.

Participants (this doc collates across small standups):
- Maya Chen (owner) — install lead
- Diego Alvarez — network/SRE support
- Priya Rao — field SE (Acadia Health)
- Samir Patel — onprem infra and drivers
- Hannah Lee — console/telemetry
- Liam O'Connor — customer escalation/CS

High-level timeline / incidents:
- 2026-11-08 (Mon morning): QubitRetail initial VPC install (v1.12.4) completed, smoke tests pass locally, but remote prefix-cache misses observed during load test. Ticket PD-980 opened.
- 2026-11-08 (Mon evening): Acadia Health on-prem install enters post-install regression — intermittent gRPC connection resets to model serving pods when sequence length > 2048.
- 2026-11-09 (Tue early): Field team applied driver rollback from nvidia-driver 535.x -> 525.x on one 3090 pool after OOMs during KV cache warm. This stabilized memory behavior but revealed TLS handshake failures for a subset of control plane connections.
- 2026-11-10 (Wed): Root cause narrowed to three correlated issues (see Observations). Canary for QubitRetail re-run; KV-cache hit-rate improved after cache-warm tuning (patch applied).

Detailed notes and triage steps:
1) KV-cache warm flakiness (QubitRetail)
- Symptom: high first-token latency on 3/10 requests during 5k rps synthetic tests; redis/backing cache shows intermittent timeouts at ~200ms.
- Hypothesis: workload pattern plus autoscaling jitter leads to cache sharding not fully rehydrated; also one sidecar (envoy) had 503 spikes under burst.
- Actions taken:
  - Diego changed envoy circuit-breaker thresholds (timeout -> 500ms -> 800ms) and added retry-on-503 for warm-up window.
  - Applied cache-warm prefetch hook in deploy config (PR link in linked_artifacts).
  - Result: after change, cold-start latency reduced by ~30% in canary.
- Open: need longer term fix to make prefix caching idempotent across pod restarts. Followup owner: Priya Rao (PD-980).

2) Kernel/driver mismatch & memory storms (Acadia Health)
- Symptom: frequent OOMs observed on GPU nodes when streaming KV cache + large-batch compilation (peak tokens ~8k).
- Investigation: Samir traced to a vendor driver bug on 535.* interacting with CUDA runtime memory reporting; swap to 525.* reduced OOM frequency.
- Mitigation: rolling rollback on affected node-pool; applied node-drain/pod-eviction script to minimize customer impact.
- Risk: 525.* has slightly worse perf on certain kernels; we saw +7% latency on long-context generation. Decision: keep 525.* until vendor patch.
- Action: Samir to open vendor escalation and attach memory allocation traces. Linked: ENG-4521.

3) TLS handshake failures after rollback (control plane)
- Symptom: ~0.8% of control-plane connections fail TLS handshake post-driver rollback window, manifesting as brief console disconnects.
- Root cause theory: NIC firmware mismatches combined with kernel module state after driver change.
- Temp fix: restart control-plane agent on affected machines (Hannah executed).
- Followup: Diego to coordinate NIC firmware audit and schedule maintenance window for firmware updates.

Customer impact notes:
- Acadia Health: intermittent user-facing retries during heavy inference sessions (SLO p95 breach observed in monitoring for a 12-hour window). CS/SE notified; customer aligned to keep the rollback and accept slight perf delta.
- QubitRetail: no customer-facing errors in production; synthetic load catches the issue. Considered low-priority but needs followup before scale.

Smoke test & validation gaps discovered:
- Our smoke harness doesn't exercise long-context (>4k) combined with streaming + batching; tests were green but missed regression.
- Need to add one long-tail scenario and a GPU stress profile in preflight.

Immediate action items (owner - ETA):
- Priya Rao — complete cache-warm idempotency PoC and add to preflight (ETA: 2026-11-15).
- Samir Patel — vendor escalation for driver bug + attach traces to ENG-4521 (ETA: 2026-11-12).
- Diego Alvarez — NIC firmware inventory and maintenance plan; propose schedule to SRE ops (ETA: 2026-11-16).
- Hannah Lee — add long-context smoke test to preflight harness; push test job to nightly (ETA: 2026-11-11).
- Maya Chen — coordinate post-install run for Acadia Health to validate rollback stability and write short KB note for field (ETA: 2026-11-12).

Notes to self / working fragments:
- TODO: update runbook with explicit driver compatibility matrix (GPU model -> driver version -> known caveats).
- Consider adding a preflight firmware check to installer (flag to block install if NIC fw < X.Y).
- Think about: rolling retries for envoy on 503 vs masking it with retry policy — prefer fixing root cause but need safe stopgap.
- Add telemetry tag on KV-cache misses to better correlate with pod restarts.

Longer-term improvements / backlog candidates:
- Circuit-breaker autoset: make envoy thresholds workload-aware on deploy.
- Cache-shard reconciliation: implement a short-lived leader-in-pod to orchestrate rehydration across scale events.
- Onboarding checklist expansion: include long-context streaming pressure test and driver validation matrix.
- Installer safety gate: validate NIC firmware and optional kernel module checks.

Open questions / unresolved
- Are we comfortable shipping 525.* driver in customer-controlled on-prem until vendor patch? (CS says yes for Acadia with documented perf delta).
- Do we need a cross-team runbook for a safe driver rollback that includes firmware checks? (SRE + release-eng input required).
- Is the KV-cache warm idempotency change safe across hybrid (VPC + onprem) topologies? (needs validation across both).

Next checkpoints:
- Daily 09:30 standup (timezone: PST) until all open action items for Acadia Health and QubitRetail are closed.
- Review meeting with release-eng and SRE on 2026-11-12 14:00 to decide on firmware maintenance window and vendor escalation cadence.

Appendix: useful links / quick references
- PD-980: QubitRetail cache-warm tickets and logs
- ENG-4521: driver memory traces and vendor escalation
- PR: infra-ops cache-warm hook (see linked_artifacts)

Quick status at close (2026-11-10):
- Critical customer-facing impact: Acadia Health (mitigated by rollback, monitoring ongoing).
- Non-blocking but high-priority: QubitRetail cache-warm; synthetic-only so no customer rollback required.
- Actions in motion: driver vendor escalation, firmware audit, preflight harness updates.

If you're picking this up: focus on Priya/Samir items first, ping me in Slack for handoff notes and I will share the memory traces folder and ssh jumplist.

--- end of notes ---
